CheckTitle: Vault auth methods bound token lifetime
Description: This check verifies that each auth method sets a **maximum lease TTL** within the configured bound (32 days by default), so tokens issued through it cannot be renewed indefinitely.
Risk: A token with an unbounded maximum TTL can be **renewed forever**, so a credential stolen from a log, a container environment or a developer machine stays valid until someone notices and revokes it explicitly. Bounded lifetimes convert theft from a permanent compromise into a time-limited one, and force the legitimate consumer to re-authenticate through the identity source you actually control.

Code.CLI:
vault auth tune -default-lease-ttl=1h -max-lease-ttl=24h kubernetes/
vault read sys/auth/kubernetes/tune
Code.Other:
1. Review each auth method's tuning with `vault read sys/auth/<path>/tune`
2. Set `default_lease_ttl` to the shortest interval the consuming workload tolerates
3. Set `max_lease_ttl` so renewal cannot extend a token indefinitely
4. Prefer short-lived tokens obtained per workload run over long-lived ones held in configuration
5. Verify applications handle token renewal and re-authentication correctly before tightening

Recommendation.Text: Tune each auth method with short default and bounded maximum lease TTLs, and confirm consuming applications re-authenticate cleanly before tightening the values.
